purpose: Normalize LTE CA, EN-DC and NR CA capability and runtime evidence at the actual band-combination/component-carrier level without promoting single-band support or UI branding into aggregation support.

evidence_levels.meaning: The combination exists in a 3GPP specification or approved change request.
An exact model/OEM/carrier source explicitly states support for the combination or capability set.
proves: device capability in the documented software/hardware context

evidence_levels.meaning: A carrier officially documents deployment/support of the combination or aggregation family.
proves: carrier-side availability in the published scope

evidence_levels.meaning: The component carriers / physical channels were observed during an actual connection.
proves: observed runtime configuration for the exact test conditions

dimensions.boundary: Display hints are branding/visualization signals and must not be treated as precise physical-channel truth.

canonical_naming_examples.note: 3GPP-style LTE CA combination example. Existence in the standard is not device support.

android_observation_methods.proves: current list of physical channel configurations
android_observation_methods.boundary: A runtime list proves only the channels exposed in that observation. It does not enumerate every combination the modem supports.
Does not identify a full standards combination by itself.

android_observation_methods.proves: carrier-policy display override such as LTE CA or NR NSA branding hint
android_observation_methods.boundary: Android explicitly states display info is for visualization/branding and is not necessarily a precise current radio state.

non_inference_rules: Single-band LTE/NR support does not prove any CA or EN-DC combination.
Two supported bands do not imply the corresponding two-band CA combination.
A standards-defined combination does not prove device support.
Device support does not prove a carrier deploys the combination.
Carrier deployment does not prove an exact device uses the combination.
LTE CA support does not prove uplink CA.
EN-DC capability does not prove a currently active NR secondary cell.
NR NSA branding does not prove a specific EN-DC combination.
5G+ / NR Advanced branding does not prove NR CA.
PhysicalChannelConfig runtime evidence does not prove the device's full capability list.
Observed component carriers at one location/time do not prove nationwide availability.
Observed DL aggregation does not imply the same UL carrier aggregation.
MIMO capability must be evidenced per band/combination when possible; do not promote a device-wide marketing MIMO claim to every component carrier.
Band-class suffixes such as A/B/C are part of the standards combination notation and must not be dropped when they materially distinguish bandwidth-class capability.
Software/baseband changes can alter exposed or usable combinations; bind runtime observations to Phase159 snapshots.
